mainTopic: When a husband can annul his wife's vows: status at the time of the vow, the two 'זה הכלל' rules, and the start of the nine women whose vows stand
overview: The משנה teaches that a husband can annul a vow his wife made while married, even if it only starts after she is widowed or divorced. It adds that once she has left his authority even for a moment, he can no longer annul her earlier vows. The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about a vow made in one status that takes effect in another, and each reads a different part of the same פסוק. רב חסדא says our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. אביי says it can even follow רבי ישמעאל, because a vow tied to a number of days has no built-in link to the marriage, unlike a vow tied to marriage or divorce. The גמרא then explains what the two 'זה הכלל' lines add: in the earlier chapter, a bride whose father's side traveled with her is still under her father, and in our chapter, a bride handed over to the husband's messengers is already in his domain. Finally, a new משנה begins listing nine young women whose vows cannot be annulled, and the list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A vow made during marriage can be annulled even if it starts after the marriage ends
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a wife vowed while under her husband's authority, he can annul it. This holds even if the vow would only start after she is widowed or divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she vowed while under her husband's authority, he can annul it for her. How so? She said, 'I am a נזירה after thirty days.' Even if she was widowed or divorced within the thirty days, the vow stays annulled.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a rule: what counts is that she made the vow while married, so the husband's annulment works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow was made while she was married, but it only kicks in after thirty days. By then she might be a widow or divorcée. The משנה says the husband's annulment, done while they were married, still holds, so the time the vow was made is what matters.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's authority over her vows
A woman who takes on נזירות

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up the question later in the סוגיא of which תנא the משנה follows.

phrases.english: If she vowed while she was under the husband's authority
he can annul it for her.
How so? She said:
"I am hereby a nazirite after thirty [days],"
phrases.notes: The משנה assumes the husband annulled this vow while they were still married.

phrases.english: even though she was widowed
or divorced within the thirty days
it is annulled.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband's annulment of a vow made during marriage holds even if the vow only takes effect after the marriage ends.

steps.title: Once she leaves his authority even briefly, he cannot annul her earlier vows
steps.stepSummary: If she vowed, was divorced, and was taken back all on the same day, the husband cannot annul. The general rule is that leaving his authority for even a moment ends his power over her earlier vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she vowed on a day, was divorced that same day, and he took her back that same day, he cannot annul. The rule is: whenever she went into her own authority for even one moment, he cannot annul.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the husband loses his power to annul, then sums it up with a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though everything happened within one day, the short break in the marriage cuts off his power over vows she made before the divorce. Taking her back does not bring that power back. The כלל makes this apply any time she was on her own, even for a moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Her own authority (not under any husband)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה cares about status: a vow made while married can be annulled, but once she has been on her own even briefly, the earlier vows are out of the husband's reach.

phrases.english: If she vowed on that day
and was divorced on that same day,
and he took her back on that same day,
he cannot annul.
This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁיָּצְאָה לִרְשׁוּת עַצְמָהּ שָׁעָה אַחַת
phrases.english: whenever she went out to her own authority for a single moment,
he cannot annul.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָדְרָה בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם וְנִתְגָּרְשָׁה בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the opposite case, where the husband loses his power to annul.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once she has been under her own authority even briefly, the husband cannot annul vows from before.

steps.title: A widow or divorcée who vows to be a nazirite once she remarries
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a widow or divorcée says she will be a נזירה once she marries, and then she marries. רבי ישמעאל says the new husband can annul. רבי עקיבא says he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A widow or divorcée who said, 'I am a נזירה for when I get married,' and then married. רבי ישמעאל says: he can annul. רבי עקיבא says: he cannot annul.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about a vow made while single that takes effect during a new marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She made the vow while on her own, but it only kicks in once she is married. רבי ישמעאל looks at when the vow takes effect, which is during the marriage, so the husband can annul. רבי עקיבא looks at when she made the vow, which was while she was single, so he cannot.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a ברייתא:
A widow or a divorcée who said:
"I am hereby a nazirite for when I will get married," and she got married,
Rabbi Yishmael says: he can annul,
and Rabbi Akiva says: he cannot annul.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: the new husband can annul. רבי עקיבא: he cannot.

steps.title: A married woman who vows to be a nazirite once she is divorced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory sign for the opinions. Then comes the reverse case: a married woman vows to be a נזירה after a divorce. רבי ישמעאל says the husband cannot annul, and רבי עקיבא says he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: The memory sign is ילל"י. A married woman who said, 'I am a נזירה for when I get divorced,' and was divorced: רבי ישמעאל says he cannot annul, and רבי עקיבא says he can.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a memory sign and then the opposite case, where the two תנאים switch sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the vow is made during marriage but takes effect after divorce. Each תנא stays consistent. רבי ישמעאל follows the time the vow takes effect, after the divorce, so the husband cannot annul. רבי עקיבא follows the time she made the vow, during the marriage, so he can.
steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים have not changed their views. Each follows his own principle, which gives opposite results in the two cases.

phrases.english: And the memory sign: Y-L-L-Y.
phrases.notes: The letters stand for יפר, לא יפר / לא יפר, יפר. In each case רבי ישמעאל's answer comes first.

phrases.english: A married woman who said:
"I am hereby a nazirite for when I will get divorced," and she was divorced,
phrases.notes: The "he" in the next lines is the husband she had when she made the vow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: he cannot annul,
and Rabbi Akiva says: he can annul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 3, with the rulings reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: the husband cannot annul a vow that takes effect after divorce. רבי עקיבא: he can.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's source: the vow's effect must be during widowhood or divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק 'the vow of a widow and divorcée' as meaning the vow itself must apply during her widowhood or divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: The פסוק says, 'And the vow of a widow and a divorcée...' This means the vow must be in effect at the time of her widowhood or divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל brings a פסוק to support his view that what matters is when the vow is in effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a widow's or divorcée's vow stands and cannot be annulled. רבי ישמעאל reads it as referring to a vow that is in effect while she is single. So a vow that is in effect during a marriage can be annulled, even if she made it while single.

keyTerms.meaning: "And the vow of a widow and a divorcée" (the פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
Behold, it says:
"And the vow of a widow and a divorcée, etc."
meaning only when the vow applies
at the time of widowhood or divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's view that the time the vow takes effect decides

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's source: the vow must be made during widowhood or divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'all that she bound upon her soul' as meaning the act of making the vow must happen during her widowhood or divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: The פסוק says, 'Everything with which she bound her soul.' This means the binding of the vow must happen at the time of her widowhood or divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא brings a different part of the same פסוק to show that what matters is when she made the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that she bound upon her soul' point to the moment she took the vow on herself. So a vow made while single cannot be annulled by a later husband. A vow made while married can still be annulled, even if it only starts after the divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: She bound upon her soul (took on the vow)
The binding of the vow, the act of vowing

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds: Behold, it says:
"All with which she has bound her soul,"
meaning only when the binding of the vow happens
at the time of widowhood or divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's view that the time of making the vow decides
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל follows when the vow takes effect. רבי עקיבא follows when the vow was made.

steps.title: רב חסדא: our משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה, which lets a husband annul a vow made during marriage that starts after divorce, follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our משנה is the view of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא links the משנה to one side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, she vowed while married and the נזירות started after the marriage ended, yet the annulment holds. That matches רבי עקיבא, who follows the time the vow was made. By רבי ישמעאל's logic, the husband could not annul a vow that takes effect after she is no longer his wife.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Our משנה is the view of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, since it looks at when the vow was made.

steps.title: אביי: the משנה can follow רבי ישמעאל, because a vow tied to days differs from one tied to marriage
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה can fit רבי ישמעאל too. The משנה's vow is tied to a number of days, while the ברייתא's vow is tied to a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל. In the משנה she tied her vow to days, and in the ברייתא she tied it to marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב חסדא and shows the משנה does not have to follow רבי עקיבא only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is what triggers the vow. In the משנה, the trigger is a fixed time ('after thirty days'), not her becoming single. In the ברייתא, the vow is built around the change in her marital status itself, and only there does רבי ישמעאל look at the later status.

keyTerms.meaning: She made her vow depend on
A teaching from the time of the משנה not included in it

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא: the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. אביי: it can follow רבי ישמעאל too, because a vow tied to days is different from one tied to a change in marital status.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Abaye said: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yishmael,
since in the משנה she made her vow depend on days,
phrases.notes: This is the "after thirty days" case from the משנה.

phrases.english: while in the ברייתא she made it depend on marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the need to limit the משנה to רבי עקיבא, as רב חסדא did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by type of condition)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה contradicts רבי ישמעאל, so it must follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow tied to a set time is different from one tied to marriage or divorce, so רבי ישמעאל can agree with the משנה.

steps.title: Finishing the difference between a days-vow and a marriage-vow
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his answer. A vow tied to a number of days might start while she is still married, or before she remarries, so it has no real link to her marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The days can run out and she is still not divorced, or the days can run out and she is still not remarried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's answer from the last step. It explains why a vow tied to a number of days is different from a vow tied to the marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא she said 'when I am divorced', so the vow is tied to the end of the marriage, and רבי ישמעאל follows the time the vow takes effect. In the משנה she said 'after thirty days'. Those days may end while she is still married, or before she remarries, so the vow is not tied to her marriage. That is why even רבי ישמעאל goes by the time she made the vow, and the husband can annul.

keyTerms.meaning: the days are finished, the set time is up

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי ישמעאל lets the husband annul a vow tied to a number of days, because those days have no built-in link to the marriage. The משנה can therefore fit both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: The days can be finished and she was not divorced,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the משנה's case, a vow that starts after a set number of days.

phrases.english: the days can be finished and she is not married.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: a vow tied to days versus a vow tied to the marriage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא thought the משנה can only follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה fits רבי ישמעאל too, because a days-vow is not linked to the marriage.

steps.title: What 'this is the principle' adds in the chapter of the betrothed young woman
steps.stepSummary: The 'זה הכלל' in the chapter 'נערה המאורסה' comes to add this case: the father, or his messengers, went along with the husband's messengers. She has not fully left her father's domain, so her father and husband annul her vows together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'this is the principle' taught in 'A betrothed young woman' comes to include a case where the father went with the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers went with the husband's messengers. In such a case, for a betrothed young woman, her father and her husband annul her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a new topic. It explains what extra case the words 'זה הכלל' add in an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה says that as long as she has not gone into the husband's domain, her father and husband annul her vows together. The words 'זה הכלל' add a case that might seem like a handover: she traveled with the husband's messengers. But her father or his messengers came along, so she is still under her father. The father and husband still annul together.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the principle, words that usually come to include an extra case
to include, to bring in an extra case
a betrothed young woman, and also the name of the earlier chapter

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different 'זה הכלל' lines here. This one is from the earlier chapter, where she is still under her father. The next step deals with the one in our chapter.

phrases.english: The "this is the principle" which is taught
in the chapter "A betrothed young woman"
phrases.notes: This is the name of an earlier chapter in נדרים. The זה הכלל line is in its משנה on דף ע״א.

phrases.aramaic: לְאֵיתוֹיֵי הָלַךְ הָאָב עִם שְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל
phrases.english: comes to include where the father went with the husband's messengers

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָלְכוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב עִם שְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: or where the father's messengers went with the husband's messengers,
regarding a betrothed young woman,
that her father and her husband annul her vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל דְּקָתָנֵי גַּבֵּי נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה לְאֵיתוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what the 'זה הכלל' lines come to add
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father or his messengers went along with the husband's messengers, she is still under her father, and both father and husband annul her vows.

steps.title: What 'this is the principle' adds in our chapter
steps.stepSummary: The 'זה הכלל' in our chapter 'ואלו נדרים' comes to add this case: the father, or his messengers, handed her over to the husband's messengers. That counts as fully going to the husband, so the husband cannot annul vows she made before.
steps.simpleTranslation: The 'this is the principle' taught in 'And these are the vows' comes to include a case where the father handed her over to the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers handed her over to the husband's messengers. In that case the husband cannot annul earlier vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second 'זה הכלל', the one in our chapter. It shows the opposite side of the case from the step before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no one from the father's side came along. She was simply handed over to the husband's messengers. That counts as entering the husband's domain, so she has left her father. Now the husband alone cannot annul vows she made before the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: the earlier ones, vows made before the marriage
'And these are the vows', the name of our chapter

steps.whatToRemember: If the father's side went along with her, she is still under her father, and the father and husband annul together. If she was handed over, she belongs to the husband's side, and he cannot annul the old vows.

phrases.english: The "this is the principle" which is taught
in the chapter "And these are the vows,"
comes to include where the father handed her over to the husband's messengers

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּסְרוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: or where the father's messengers handed her over to the husband's messengers,
that the husband cannot annul the earlier vows.
phrases.notes: 'The earlier vows' means vows she made before she was married.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל דְּקָתָנֵי גַּבֵּי וְאֵלּוּ נְדָרִים לְאֵיתוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The matching opposite case to step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Handing her over to the husband's messengers counts as entering the husband's domain, so he cannot annul vows made before the marriage.

steps.title: New משנה: nine young women whose vows stand
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. It lists nine young women whose vows cannot be annulled. The first cases are a grown woman who is an orphan, and a young woman who grew up and is an orphan.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are nine young women whose vows stand. The first is a grown woman who is an orphan. The second is a young woman who then became grown, and she is an orphan.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a list of nine women whose vows no one can annul. Only the first two cases appear here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father can annul only while she is a נערה, and a husband can annul only her vows during the marriage. A בוגרת who is a יתומה has no father with any power over her, and no husband either. So nobody can annul her vow. The second case is the same, except she made the vow as a נערה and then grew up.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה, marking a new משנה
they stand, they stay in force
a grown woman, past the age of נערה
an orphan, here meaning her father is not alive
and she grew up, she reached the age of a בוגרת

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Nine young women, their vows stand:
A grown woman, and she is an orphan.
A young woman who grew up, and she is an orphan.
phrases.notes: She made the vow while still a young woman, and then she grew up.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine kinds of young women have vows that cannot be annulled, starting with an orphan who is a בוגרת, or an orphan who was a נערה and then became a בוגרת.
